expected_behavior: Tyler EagleWeb self-service portal (kingscountyca-web.tylerhost.net) exposes a document-number/APN/grantor-grantee "Official Records" search for real property recorded documents, matching the pattern already confirmed working for Kern/Butte/Lake.
observed_behavior: Disclaimer accept succeeds with NO CAPTCHA (GET+POST both return HTTP 200; disclaimerAccepted session cookie is set cleanly -- this is NOT a Fresno/Tehama-style reCAPTCHA wall). However the portal's home menu (POST /web/homeActions) and every action group tested (ACTIONGROUP201S1/S2/S3/S5, ACTIONGROUP483S1, wizard/COPYREQUEST400S1, fraudGuard/disclaimerPage) exposes ONLY Clerk-office record types: Vital Records Certified Copies, Marriage License Application, Fictitious Business Names Application, Professional Registrations, Clerk Records Search (CEQA filings / FBN / Notary / Registration sub-searches, DOCSEARCH201S1/S6/S9/S11), Military Discharge (DD-214) copies, and Owner/Fraud Alert. No "Official Records Search" / real-property deed search action group exists anywhere in this instance's menu tree. Corroborated by web search: Kings County's own published guidance states that per CA Assembly Bill 1785 the office no longer provides online access to recorded document indexes or APN-linked searches -- document copies are in-person at the Government Center or by mail/public-records request only. The county's legacy self-hosted portal (http://publicrecords.countyofkings.com/) is unreachable (connection timeout, no response).
impact: Cannot perform parcel-tied recorder verification (grantor/grantee/deed confirmation) for any Kings County parcel through any online channel. Under the pipeline's verified-or-excluded standard, no both-sites-verified dossier can be produced for Kings at this time via automated or even manual-browser online means.
current_handling: Kings dossier generation stopped for this session before any parcel processing began. Zero dossiers produced for Kings. Assessor (MPTS) confirmed live and usable for value/situs data only -- but assessor-only data can never satisfy the both-sites standard on its own.

expected_behavior: The county-name-assessor-data-access-58.csv note ('TDLS 164, dated March 31 2026, not yet opened') implied an upcoming/current sale to build pre-auction dossiers against.
observed_behavior: TDLS164's sale actually ran March 20-31, 2026, which is already in the past as of this session (2026-08-08). Cross-referencing the full 311-parcel non-redeemed list against the live recorder showed 178 of 311 (57%) had already sold (Deed Tax recorded) and 111 of 311 (36%) had been redeemed (Release of Lien recorded) since the list was published -- only 17 of 311 (5%) remained genuinely still tax-defaulted with no release or sale-deed found. No next sale (TDLS165) has been published by Lake County yet.
impact: Using the TDLS164 list at face value without a live per-parcel recorder recheck would have produced dossiers that were wrong (redeemed or already sold) for 93% of parcels on the list -- a direct repeat of the kind of trust failure this pipeline already suffered once.
current_handling: Resolved by building a real recorder-based lien-lifecycle classifier (lake/lake_recorder_lien_check.py) and only shipping the 16 (of 17, minus the one discrepancy above) parcels with live, dated recorder evidence of an unreleased, unsold tax lien. signal_priority.get_signal('lake') was left untouched (not modified, not overridden) -- it correctly falls through to the shared NO_SCHEDULED_AUCTION / 'No scheduled auction -- monitor for a future sale date' signal since lake is not in AUCTION_CALENDAR.
